# components/reveal

Import: `import { Reveal, RevealGroup, Parallax, LazySection } from "@tundralibs/ui/reveal"`

Rendered in every variant on the catalogue (`deno task build:demos`, then `demo/index.html`). Guides: [Getting started](../UI-Getting-Started.md) · [rAPId integration](../UI-Rapid.md) · [Theming](../UI-Theming.md).

## Functions

### `Reveal`

```ts
Reveal(props: RevealProps): Html
```

Content that reveals itself as it scrolls into view. Hidden only under
`html.js` (a page without the script shows everything at once);
reveal.js adds `is-revealed` when the block enters the viewport, so the
effect never costs a plain page anything. Blocks already on screen at
load reveal immediately.

### `RevealGroup`

```ts
RevealGroup(props: RevealGroupProps): Html
```

A row or list of blocks that reveal one after another.

### `Parallax`

```ts
Parallax(props: ParallaxProps): Html
```

A block that drifts against the scroll — a hero image, a decorative
panel. reveal.js moves it with a transform while it is on screen,
throttled to animation frames. It stays still under reduced motion and
on coarse pointers (phones): a transform per scroll frame on a phone
fights the browser's own scroll compositing and judders. Overflow is
the caller's to clip: give the parent `overflow: hidden` or let the
block bleed.

### `LazySection`

```ts
LazySection(props: LazySectionProps): Html
```

A section that loads when it is about to be seen, not on page load — a
long landing page's lower bands. With the rAPId runtime on the page
reveal.js calls `window.rapid.swap(action, section)` as it nears the
viewport (unlike `data-load`, which fetches on mount). On a plain page
there is no runtime: the section keeps its placeholder, so give it
content worth keeping (static sections need no loading at all) —
reveal.js marks it `data-lazy-inert` and moves on.

## Types

### `RevealEffect`

How a revealed block arrives: fade in place, rise from below, grow from 96%, or sharpen from a blur.

- `"fade"`
- `"rise"`
- `"scale"`
- `"blur"`

### `RevealDelay`

A delay before the reveal plays, in steps of 80 ms (classes, never an inline style).

- `"0"`
- `"1"`
- `"2"`
- `"3"`

### `RevealTag`

The element the reveal renders as.

- `"div"`
- `"section"`
- `"li"`
- `"span"`

### `RevealProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `Html` | yes |  |
| `effect` | `RevealEffect` |  |  |
| `delay` | `RevealDelay` |  |  |
| `once` | `boolean` |  | Reveal once and stay (default). `false` hides it again when it scrolls out, so it replays on the way back. |
| `tag` | `RevealTag` |  |  |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

### `RevealGroupProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `Html[]` | yes | Each item becomes its own `Reveal`. |
| `effect` | `RevealEffect` |  |  |
| `stagger` | `boolean` |  | Stagger the items: reveal.js numbers each child (`--reveal-index`, through the CSSOM) and the stylesheet delays it by that many steps. |
| `once` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `tag` | `"div" | "ul"` |  | The group element. @default "div" |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

### `ParallaxSpeed`

How far a parallax block drifts against the scroll: a tenth, a fifth or a third of the distance.

- `"slow"`
- `"medium"`
- `"fast"`

### `ParallaxProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `content` | `Html` | yes |  |
| `speed` | `ParallaxSpeed` |  |  |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

### `LazySectionProps`

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | yes | Required: the swapped region keeps this id. |
| `action` | `string` | yes | The fragment URL rAPId fetches once the section nears the viewport. |
| `placeholder` | `Html` | yes | What shows until then — a Skeleton, or static content a plain page keeps. |
| `rootMargin` | `string` |  | How far ahead of the viewport to fetch. @default "200px 0px" |
| `attrs` | `Attrs` |  |  |

## Usage

Each example as the rAPId call and the HTML it renders — the markup a plain page writes by hand. Icons are inline SVG in the real output; they are shortened to `<svg …>…</svg>` here.

### A section that rises into view

Hidden only under `html.js`; a page without the script shows it at once.

```ts
Reveal({
  content: html`
    <h2>Why teams switch</h2>
  `,
  effect: "rise",
  tag: "section",
})
```

```html
<section class="reveal" data-reveal="rise">
  <h2>Why teams switch</h2>
</section>
```

### Three cards, one after another

```ts
RevealGroup({
  items: ["Send", "Chase", "Collect"].map((t) =>
    Card({
      title: t,
      body: html`
        <p>…</p>
      `,
    })
  ),
  stagger: true,
})
```

```html
<div class="reveal-group" data-reveal-group="" data-reveal-stagger="">
  <div class="reveal" data-reveal="rise">
    <div class="card">
      <div class="card__content">
        <div class="card__header">
          <div class="card__heading">
            <div class="card__title">Send</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="card__body">
          <p>…</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="reveal" data-reveal="rise">
    <div class="card">
      <div class="card__content">
        <div class="card__header">
          <div class="card__heading">
            <div class="card__title">Chase</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="card__body">
          <p>…</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="reveal" data-reveal="rise">
    <div class="card">
      <div class="card__content">
        <div class="card__header">
          <div class="card__heading">
            <div class="card__title">Collect</div>
          </div>
        </div>
        <div class="card__body">
          <p>…</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```

### A band that loads as it nears the viewport

With the rAPId runtime the section swaps in `/fragments/customers`; a plain page keeps the placeholder.

```ts
html`
  ${Parallax({
    content: html`
      <img src="/img/texture.png" width="1200" height="400" alt="">
    `,
    speed: "slow",
  })}${LazySection({ id: "customers", action: "/fragments/customers", placeholder: SkeletonCard() })}
`
```

```html
<div class="parallax" data-parallax="0.1">
  <img src="/img/texture.png" width="1200" height="400" alt="">
</div>
<section class="lazy-section" id="customers" data-lazy-section="" data-action="/fragments/customers">
  <div class="skeleton-card" aria-busy="true">
    <span class="skeleton skeleton--block" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="skeleton skeleton--title" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="skeleton skeleton--text skeleton--w-full" aria-hidden="true"></span>
    <span class="skeleton skeleton--text skeleton--w-half" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  </div>
</section>
```

## CSS hooks

Classes defined by `components/reveal/reveal.css` — structural, token-driven; override from an unlayered stylesheet (see [Theming](../UI-Theming.md)):

`.is-revealed`, `.js`, `.lazy-section`, `.parallax`, `.reveal`, `.reveal--delay-1`, `.reveal--delay-2`, `.reveal--delay-3`, `.reveal-group`

## Behaviour

`components/reveal/reveal.js` ships in `ui.js` (delegated on `document`, re-initialised after a rAPId swap).

Attributes it reads or writes: `data-action`, `data-lazy-inert`, `data-lazy-loading`, `data-lazy-margin`, `data-lazy-section`, `data-parallax`, `data-reveal`, `data-reveal-repeat`, `data-reveal-stagger`.

Events: `rapid:swapped`.
